result.final_text:
## What this letter says
A specialist saw you for bleeding from the rectum (rectal bleeding). It comes and goes. It does not cause pain. You have not lost weight.

The specialist wrote to your doctor. The letter says three things need to be ruled out. Ruled out means checked for.
- Colon cancer is possible. It has not been confirmed.
- Colon polyps are possible. They have not been confirmed.
- Hemorrhoids are possible. The letter says they are the most likely cause.

The letter says you are often constipated (chronically constipated). Your blood pressure was 130/70. Your heart rate was 75. Your breathing rate was 16. Your belly was soft and not tender.

The letter also says you have no weight loss, no nausea and no vomiting. You have a good appetite. You have no night sweats, no fevers and no chills. You have no known allergies.

## What you need to do
1. Have a full colonoscopy exam. The letter says this is because of your age.
2. Have a CBC (complete blood count) blood test. It counts blood cells. It will be checked and monitored.
3. The colonoscopy will be set up at Sample Hospital. The full report goes to your doctor's office.
4. Do not stop or change your medicine unless your doctor tells you to. The letter does not say it is changing.

## Dates and medicines
- The letter gives no date or time for the colonoscopy.
- The letter gives no date or time for the CBC blood test.
- The letter does not say if the CBC has been done already.
- Cardizem CD, 240 mg. The letter does not say how often you take it. Keep taking it. The letter does not change it.
- You also take eye drops. The letter does not name them.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- When will my colonoscopy be? When will I get the date?
- When and where do I have the CBC blood test? Has it been done?
- What is a colonoscopy, and what happens during it?
- How often should I take Cardizem CD?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
